title: Policy, privilege and security govern strategy without weakening requirements
summary: Deployment requirements state what must be true; policy states which strategies are permitted. Privilege is explicit rather than an implicit sudo prefix. Security includes content hashes, argument boundaries, secret redaction and provenance failure behavior.
invariants: Never silently weaken a requirement because the preferred installation strategy is unavailable.
System packages, portable binaries, compilation and network download are independent policy choices.
Do not casually prepend sudo; seek a permitted user-local strategy or fail.
Do not log secrets in ordinary deployment evidence.
Do not download arbitrary replacements merely because a dependency is missing.
Fail closed when required provenance or final state cannot be established.

provenance.claim: Defines fail-closed behavior, strategy policy and explicit privilege.
